stories.headline: Opposition-controlled legislature passes NT$780B defense bill, cutting Lai's request by 38%; US expresses disappointment and concern
stories.summary: Taiwan's KMT and TPP used their legislative majority to pass a NT$780 billion (US$24.8B) special defense spending bill on May 8, approximately two-thirds of the NT$1.25 trillion requested by President Lai Ching-te, after a 162-day standoff. The U.S. State Department called the cuts a 'concession' to China and said it was 'disappointed,' while the DPP accused the opposition of helping aggressors 'demolish Taiwan's defenses'; a separate intelligence source said the PLA's assessment that the 'hellscape' deterrence strategy would thwart invasion likely informed Beijing's effort to block the budget.

stories.headline: Lai completes Eswatini state visit after China-linked airspace denials forced southern Indian Ocean detour
stories.summary: President Lai Ching-te completed a state visit to Eswatini — Taiwan's sole African ally — from approximately May 2–5, arriving via an unannounced 'arrive then announce' method after a prior April attempt was blocked when three African countries (Seychelles, Mauritius, Madagascar) revoked overflight permits; his return flight took a near-maximum-range southern detour over the Indian Ocean. stories.headline: TSMC reports record April revenue up 17.5% year-on-year as AI demand sustains semiconductor boom
stories.summary: TSMC reported consolidated revenue of NT$410.73 billion for April 2026, its highest-ever April figure and a 17.5% increase from a year earlier, though down 1.1% from March; cumulative revenue for the first four months of 2026 rose 29.9% year-on-year to NT$1.54 trillion. Analysts attributed growth to sustained AI chip demand from hyperscalers, with TSMC having raised its full-year guidance in April.

stories.summary: Taiwan's Legislative Yuan passed amendments establishing mandatory nurse-to-patient ratios, with the KMT and TPP versions prevailing; the DPP had proposed a different consultation mechanism.
